name: night1-hill/index
title: Visiting Hours: Night 1, Larch Street on a hill
subtitle: Layout A's four routes laid on a slope, as you offered: Walt's bike shop at the bottom by the creek, the house with its tower at the top, four terraces 12 m apart. The plan first, then the stills from the bottom, the middle and the top.
questions: Does the hill show the size of the setting? From the far bank you see the whole climb; from the lookout at the top you see the whole street.

Keep the gold beacon? The tower alone is hidden from most of the climb (you walk under 12 m retaining walls), so a soft column of light stands up out of it: with it the house is found from 74 to 100% of every route. Without it, the tower shows from 0 to 18% of the way.

Is any route too long or too short? The road takes about 32 s (two switchbacks, 308 m), the garden stairs 10 s, the rooftops 12 s (nine double jumps), the creek ravine 30 s (the culvert slide, 28 falls). The way in, from the arrival over the creek and through the shop to Walt, takes about 4 s.
notes: Both halves of Walt's optional premise ('the same Saturday') are below his gate: the neighbours' loop plays on the far bank where you arrive, and Saturday's paper is on his yard bench.
The flood wall along the creek is drawn low so the climb shows from the far bank; the dream holds it higher than it looks, so the shop's apron is the only landing.
Every line is a placeholder; the shop's sign has no lettering.
